item.title: Sanja Matsuri — Guide
item.description: The Sanja Matsuri, held over a weekend in mid-May at Asakusa Shrine beside Senso-ji Temple, is one of Tokyo’s three great Shinto festivals and among the largest, wildest and most exciting in the city. Honouring the three founders of Senso-ji, it draws around 1.5 to 2 million people over three days and centres on the boisterous parading of mikoshi — ornate portable shrines believed to house the deities. Around a hundred mikoshi from the local neighbourhoods, plus three huge main shrines, are hoisted onto the shoulders of teams of chanting, tightly-packed bearers and carried, bouncing and swaying, through the crowded streets in an electric, high-energy atmosphere.
